runtime: the monster table (X $0400, Y $04C0, kind $0580, flags $0640, Death's drain $0700), built from each level by objects_place; pinn232 would also use $0400-$040D as work bytes
never written: the emulator's power-on pattern; no file loads here

runtime: the 32 x 32 tile grid, built from the level file by level_build and changed in play
never written: the power-on pattern between DATATITLE and PINN232

runtime: copies made at load by heroes_load_shapes: $1800-$1BFF the heroes' shot shapes, which each level start puts back at $7600 and $7E00, and $1C00-$1FFF the PLYRS.SPR shapes they replaced, which nothing reads
runtime: the 64 x 64 colour map ($2000) and character map ($3000), drawn from the tile grid by grid_draw and changed in play (PLYRS.SPR loads here first and is copied away)
runtime: the two screens and their sprite pointers, drawn by maze_draw and the panel routines
never written: the power-on pattern after PLAYER-$E000
never written: the power-on pattern after DATATREASURE
never written: the power-on pattern after DITTIDATA
never written: the power-on pattern above OBJDIS
extra: the fonts and sprite shapes: GAUNT CHR $4800 and the PLYRS.SPR shapes copied to $7000

comments.text: Level 1's file as it loads into the level buffer ($0A00, file LEVEL 001): the file's length less 2 ($4F), with bit 7 of $0A02 as its ninth bit. A longer level file fills more of the buffer.

The level header's flags: bit 7 the maze wraps left and right, bit 6 top and bottom, bit 0 shots hurt the other player, bit 1 they stun, bit 2 only one exit (at random), bits 3-5 the maze's look (maze_style). Level 1 has none.
The level header's wall colour in bits 3-5 (maze_style_colours) and the length's ninth bit in bit 7.
How many bytes of wall commands follow the header ($0A in level 1).

Level 1's wall commands ($0A04-$0A0D): a pair starts a line at a tile (kind in the first byte's top three bits, column and row in the low five), each byte after it extends the line (direction in the top three bits, length - 1 in the low five).
The second byte of the wall commands, which wall_same_kind and wall_start read as a pair with the first.

Level 1's objects ($0A0E-$0A50): run-length coded tiles from the top-left of the grid (a byte from $80 skips tiles, a smaller one is a tile, repeated when the byte after it is below $13); tiles from $40 are monsters, $3F the players' start.

The file DATATITLE 244, left at $1000 by the title and selection programs (which load it at $6400 and move it): tune data for the music player at $E000, the title music, 18 seconds long. The play program never plays it; the BIT instructions at $9CE2 (power_shot) and $AC65, which hide a load from the code before them, read its byte at $10A9 and the value goes unused.
A byte inside DATATITLE whose address is also the operand of the BITs at $9CE2 and $AC65, which hide an instruction; those BITs read it and nothing uses the result. The tune data goes on.

The file PINN232 5000: a cable link for moving memory between this machine and another through the user port, called from BASIC (SYS 5000 receives a block, SYS 5003 receives several, SYS 5006 sends one). The game loads it with its other files and never calls it; it looks like a tool the developers used and left on the disk. Three JMPs: 5000, 5003, 5006.
SYS 5003,n: receives n blocks, each to the address its own header gives.

SYS 5006,address,length: sends the block: a nine-byte header from $0402 (its first byte 3, then the length and the address), then the bytes, with the screen blanked and interrupts off; the border colour changes with each byte.

Sends one byte, inverted, as a frame of bits: each bit is put on CIA 2 port A bit 2 (user port PA2) after the other side has signalled on port B bit 6, with a short delay between bits; the border colour steps on.
A short delay (12 loops) between bits.

Takes a number from the BASIC statement into A (low byte, from $65) and Y (high, from $64), by calling two BASIC ROM routines, $AE86 and $BC9B. What those do was not checked here: the snapshot holds the RAM beneath the ROM, where the game has its own code.

SYS 5000,address: receives a block. The nine-byte header comes first, into $0402; a non-zero address from the statement replaces the header's; then the bytes, to that address, with the screen blanked and interrupts off.
The block receive for an address in A/Y (pinn_receive_many calls it with 0, the header's own address).

Receives one byte: raises the handshake on port B bit 1, waits for the start bit on port B bit 0, then shifts in the bits from port B bit 0 into $040B, and inverts the result; the border colour steps on.
A short delay (13 loops) between received bits.
A longer delay (256 short ones) before a block is sent.
The rest of the file PINN232 5000 after its code: 141 bytes in the pattern of unwritten memory, saved with it.

The first of the three maze fonts (font select 2, from the file GAUNT CHR $4800): 256 multicolour glyphs. $00 is the floor and $01-$5A the maze's other pieces (the walls' brick joins, doors, treasure, food, potions, keys, generators, the trap, the transporter, the exits), four glyphs to a tile (tile_chars). $5B looks like floor and marks a cell as occupied (cell_mark). The rest are the monsters, four glyphs to a facing: the lobber $5C-$5F (one picture for every facing), ghosts $60-$7F, grunts $80-$9F, demons $A0-$BF, sorcerers $C0-$DF, Death $E0-$FF. panel_flash cycles the three fonts, which differ in the monsters' glyphs, so every monster on screen animates at once.
Glyphs 1-12 of the first maze font, which maze_style rewrites per level from one of the style blocks at $6408-$6567 (the walls' look).
Glyphs $2E and $2F of the first maze font, which hidden_potion_place rewrites with the hidden potion's picture.
The first maze font's glyphs $80-$FF: grunts, demons, sorcerers and Death, frame one.
The second maze font (font select 4): the same maze pieces with the monsters in their second frame.
Glyphs 1-12 of the second maze font, rewritten by maze_style.
The hidden potion's glyphs in the second maze font.
The second maze font's glyphs $80-$FF: grunts, demons, sorcerers and Death, frame two.
The third maze font (font select 6): the monsters in their third frame.
Glyphs 1-12 of the third maze font, rewritten by maze_style.
The hidden potion's glyphs in the third maze font.
The third maze font's glyphs $80-$FF: grunts, demons, sorcerers and Death, frame three.

The panel and message font (font select 8 at $6000, hires): glyph n draws ASCII n + $20 for letters and digits; its own glyphs are the inventory icons ($01-$0F), SCORE ($1A-$1F), ELF ($3B-$3E), the GAUNTLET logo ($40-$6F), WARRIOR ($70-$77), and the big letters of the LEVEL and TREASURE ROOM titles (top halves from $C1, bottom halves from $E1).
The panel font's glyphs $80-$FF; maze_style takes its wall styles from here ($6408, $6468, $6508) and hidden_potion_place its potion pictures ($6580).
One of maze_style's 96-byte wall styles.
The six special potions' pictures, 16 bytes (two glyphs) each, for hidden_potion_place.

Sprite shapes $A0-$BF (in video bank 1): $A0 the solid block the side masks use, $A1 a short bar, $A2-$AB the digits 0-9 (the level number and the treasure clock), $AC-$AF a lobbed rock rising, $B0-$B5 growing clouds, $B6-$B7 striped bars, $B8-$BF a fireball in eight directions.
Shapes $B0-$BF: the clouds, the bars and (from $6E00) the fireball, which the start-up copied there from $7400.
The fireball's eight shapes ($B8-$BF), copied here from the font file at load (shapes_7400_to_6E00).
The last four fireball shapes.

Player one's hero's sprite shapes $C0-$DF, copied from PLYRS.SPR at load (hero_copy_chars): $C0-$D7 walking, eight facings in three frames (anim_frames 0, 8, 16), and $D8-$DF the hero's shot in eight directions (put back from $1800 at each level start).
The hero's shapes from $C0 + 32 bytes on: the rest of the first walking frames.
Shapes $D0-$D7, the hero's third walking frame.
Shapes $D4-$D7.
Shapes $D8-$DF: player one's hero's shot in eight directions, put here from $1800 at each level start (shapes_from_1800); the end of exit_spin shows them as the player shrinking into the exit.
The last four of player one's shot shapes.
Player two's hero's sprite shapes $E0-$FF, laid out like player one's: $E0-$F7 walking, $F8-$FF the shot.
Shapes $F0-$F7: player two's third walking frame.
Shapes $F8-$FF: player two's shot in eight directions.
The last four of player two's shot shapes.
The game's entry, where the selection program's JMP $8000 lands: a jump over thirteen zero bytes to the start-up at $8013.
Thirteen zero bytes between the entry jump and the start-up; nothing in the game reads them.

The start-up, run once after the hand-over. Turns the music player off, sets level_number to 1 and installs the interrupts. Unless the files are already in (heroes_loaded), hands the interrupts to the KERNAL, blanks the screen, loads all eight files (load_files), takes the interrupts back and picks level 8's file at random. Then starts CIA 1's timers, blanks the screen, copies the heroes' graphics (heroes_load_shapes), clears the screens, starts the tune player, resets the sound effects, starts the side masks, resets the game (game_reset), waits, sets multicolour text, video bank 1 and screen $4000, calls vic_font with 8 (which its AND #$07 turns into character base 0, $4000: the panel's font, $6000, is set each frame by the raster interrupt at $8623), colours the panel, sets the treasure-room countdown to 5, shows the screen, and falls into game_start.

A new game: clears the screens, counts from level 1, waits for a first player to press fire (wait_first_player), draws the panel and its digits, and goes on to the first level (level_begin). game_over_check comes back here when every player is gone.

Starts a level: no scroll, the pass counter cleared, the screen cleared; loads the level (level_start), builds it (level_build), picks the exits (exits_pick_one), moves Death to the front (deaths_first), draws the grid, sets the special exits, draws the monsters, hides a potion and scatters the extras, places the screen and players (level_place_players), restores the heroes' shapes (shapes_from_1800), sets the fine scrolls and the screens, draws the maze, moves the monsters once, waits for line $70 and plays sound 3; then runs the treasure-room loop ($8120) for a treasure room or the play loop ($818B) for any other level.

One pass of a treasure room: waits for line $40, redraws the maze and its colours, counts the pass ($824B), fires and moves the shots against tiles, players and monsters, and on a pass with no change of scroll starts the room's tune (treasure_start), the pickups and the panel; then joins, the amulet, the clock (treasure_clock) and the leave timers. When the clock runs out the room ends (treasure_end); when every player in it has left by its exit, the next level begins.

One pass of an ordinary level: waits for line $40, redraws the maze and its colours, counts the pass ($824B), fires the players' shots, and on a pass with no change of scroll: the shots against tiles, players and monsters, the magic keys, the generators, the monsters, a pending trap, the pickups, the doors, the panel, the amulet, the idle timer, joining players and the leave timers. While a player in the game has not left, it loops; then game_over_check, and the next level.
Part of the play loop (the scroll test). Its address is also the operand of a BIT at $CE68 that hides an instruction, which is why it carries a symbol.
Sets the frame flag $8264 and waits for raster line $40 (wait_raster); clears $8248. Used between steps of the start-up and screen changes to let a frame pass.

Resets per-level state before play starts: all sprites enabled in the copy $9111, the two players' status bytes $9120/$9121 cleared of bits 6 and 7, $912C/$912D set to $C0/$E0, and the counters at $B66B/$B66C, $AF38-$AF3B, $B4E7, $B4E9 and $B65A cleared; $B65B is reloaded from $B65C.
Counted up by the raster interrupt every frame; wait_64_frames waits on it, and routines use it to run every fourth or 64th frame.
A second frame counter, cleared by wait_frame_40.
Set while the tune player should run from the raster interrupt (level_intro, treasure_start).
The monster slot being handled.
Counts the main loop's passes in a level; monsters_run, generators_run and others use its low bits to spread their work over passes.
Counted up every frame by the raster interrupt; exit_enter clears $824C,x (this and the next byte) for a player going into an exit.
Counted up every frame with $824C.
The index of the last monster in the table ($FF for none): up to $BF, 192 monsters.
The screen being shown, as $D018's high nibble: $00 for $4000, $10 for $4400.
The maze font, as $D018's bits 1-3: 2, 4 or 6 ($4800, $5000, $5800), cycled by panel_flash; 8 for the panel font at $6000 on the message screens.
The value raster_arm writes to $D011 (with the fine scroll ORed in); display_on and display_off set its bit 4.
panel_flash's countdown between font changes.
panel_flash's step through the font cycle.
The maze font selects panel_flash cycles through: 2 4 2 6 (then a spare 0).
The maze's second colour ($D022), dark grey $0B, white during a potion's blast.
A work byte many routines use.
A second work byte.
A third work byte (direction bits in the scroll and wall tests).
The directions the walls block for the player being moved (block_dirs).
Raised when the screen has scrolled a whole cell; the raster interrupt then lets the main loop redraw ($8264).
Read and cleared with redraw_due by the raster interrupt; nothing in the traced code sets it.
A copy of freeze_p1 taken when the players are read.
Set when a coarse scroll step has finished; scroll_decide waits on it.
scroll_decide's countdown while nothing scrolls.
The raster interrupt's go-ahead for the main loop (wait_raster waits on it).
A spare byte after main_go.
The scroll's X in 2-pixel units: the world X of the screen's left edge.
The scroll's Y in 2-pixel units.

The hardware IRQ handler ($FFFE). Saves A, X and Y; when the video chip reports a raster interrupt it jumps through $0314 to whichever raster handler the chain has installed (raster_masks, raster_frame); any other interrupt returns at once through irq_exit.
Common exit of every interrupt handler: restores Y, X and A and returns from the interrupt.
The NMI handler ($FFFA): a bare RTI, so RESTORE does nothing during play.

Installs the game's own interrupt handling: masks both CIAs' interrupts and acknowledges them, points the hardware IRQ vector $FFFE at irq_entry ($8268) and the NMI vector $FFFA at nmi_rti ($827F), sets the processor port to $35 (RAM at $A000 and $E000, I/O at $D000), enables the raster interrupt, starts the mask-sprite chain (sprites_init_masks), re-enables interrupts and restarts CIA 1's timers (cia_timers_start). Called twice by the start-up and from $99FD.

Hands interrupts back to the KERNAL before a disk load: masks both CIAs, stops their timers, sets CIA 1's timer A latch to $4025, disables the raster interrupt and every sprite, clears the sprite-enable copy $9111, points $0314 at the KERNAL's $EA31 and banks the KERNAL ROM in ($01 = $36). irq_install undoes it.
Fills colour RAM ($D800-$DBFF) and both screens ($4000-$47FF) with zero.
The last column of each player's panel block in the panel rows: $0F for player one, $1F for player two.
Four bytes beside panel_columns: $00 $10 $0F $1F. $832D,x is read by $A655 and $B9E9, and $832F by $B90D.

The column of the first potion icon in each player's block ($0F and $1F): potion_take puts a new potion's icon at $439C + this less the potions already held, so icons fill leftwards from here, and potion_drop clears the last one.

The status panel's text, ASCII with the panel font's own glyphs: four sixteen-byte rows of hero names, in hero order 0 Warrior (glyphs $90-$97, drawn as one word), 1 Valkyrie, 2 Wizard, 3 Elf (glyphs $5B-$5E). panel_draw_players picks the row with the hero number times sixteen.
" SCORE  HEALTH ": the SCORE word is the panel font's glyphs $3A-$3F.
" 000000   2000 ": the score and health a player starts with, as the panel shows them.
Sixteen spaces, the panel's fourth row.
The four rows panel_press_fire_draw puts in an empty player's block, as glyph numbers: the GAUNTLET logo (glyphs $41-$5F) and "PRESS FIRE" ($30 $32 $25 $33 $33, $26 $29 $32 $25).
The second row of panel_press_fire: the logo's lower half.
The third row of panel_press_fire: the logo's tail.
The fourth row of panel_press_fire: "PRESS FIRE".
Eighty bytes after panel_press_fire: the same logo and PRESS FIRE rows again, with $40 in place of $00 and $20. Nothing in the traced code reads them.

Draws the status panel for each player who is in the game ($9120,x not zero) and whose pair $B663,x/$B665,x is zero: four rows of sixteen characters from the hero's name row (hero_names, sixteen bytes per hero, chosen by $911C,x), the SCORE/HEALTH legend, the starting digits and a blank row, each byte less $20 (the panel font draws ASCII less $20), into the panel at $4324 + the player's column ($832B,x: $0F for player one, $1F for player two). Then points sprites 2-7 at shape $A1 ($43FA-$43FF).
The low byte of the hero_names address in panel_draw_players' first LDA, rewritten with the hero's row.
The high byte of that address, rewritten too; the rest of panel_draw_players' copy loop follows.
For each player not in the game ($9120,x zero), copies panel_press_fire's four rows of sixteen glyphs into that player's block of the panel (column from panel_columns).

Sets the maze's background colours ($D021 black, $D022 dark grey $0B, $D023 white) and colours each active player's panel block with the hero's colour (hero_colours, $9114) in colour RAM $DB20-$DBBF; sets the sprite multicolours ($D025 light red $0A, $D026 white).
The Y position of the two side-mask sprites in each of the four raster bands: $2E, $58, $82, $AC.
The raster line of the first mask band, $2A.
The raster line of each next mask band's interrupt: $54, $7E, $A0, $CB; the last is where raster_frame takes over.
Which of the four mask bands raster_masks is on (0-3).

Sets up the two black side masks: sprites 0 and 1 in colour 0 at X $1F and $138, stretched vertically, both pointing at the solid shape $A0 ($6800) in either screen ($43F8/$43F9, $47F8/$47F9); enables the sprites in $9111; arms CIA 1's interrupts, waits for a frame and starts the raster chain (raster_arm).

The raster handler that follows the mask bands, entered on alternate interrupts through $864C. On one: acknowledges, steps the frame counters $8247/$8248, calls $B933 on every 64th frame or whenever $C40C/$C40D is not zero, then $B977 and frame_tasks; raises the main loop's flag $8264 and resets $D022 from $825A when a coarse scroll step has finished ($825F/$8260); re-arms the chain (raster_arm); calls $92BF, $915C and $91CC; restores the colours $D021/$D023; calls $A036 when $8249 is set, and $CCD3. On the other (b_85FB): waits for line $CF, blanks the display, turns off the sprites and their colours, switches $D018 to the panel ($08: screen $4000, font $6000), and at line $D6 sets 25-row text mode and 40-column hires ($D016 $18) for the status panel; then asks for line $F8.
Toggled by raster_frame on each entry: 0 runs the frame work, 1 the panel split.
The work done once a frame from the raster interrupt: panel_flash $8C7C, $9274, $A768, $92D9, scroll_step, scroll_decide, scroll_limit.
Raster handler for the side masks: moves sprites 0 and 1 to the next band's Y (mask_y) and asks for the next band's line (mask_lines); after the fourth band points $0314 at raster_frame.

Starts the frame's raster chain: points $0314 at raster_masks, asks for line mask_first_line, sets $D011 from $8252 and the vertical scroll $882E, $D016 to multicolour with the horizontal scroll $882F, enables the raster interrupt, and sets $D018 from the screen in front ($8250) and the maze font ($8251).
Six bytes no traced code reaches: SEI, JSR wait_frame_40, CLI, RTS.

Stops the screen scrolling in a direction the two players disagree on: with both sticks' direction bits ($8EB2, $8EB3) XORed, a vertical (or horizontal) pair that differs in both bits marks that axis as not to scroll in scroll_dir ($8837 bits 0-1 or 2-3 set).

Decides this frame's scrolling and reads the players. With no scroll asked (scroll_dir $0F) it counts $8263 down, raising $825F every fourth frame, and reads the players every eighth. With a scroll asked it returns until the coarse step in progress is done ($8262), adjusts the vertical fine scroll on the diagonals 9 and 6, then reads the players: notes the map position ($8831/$8833 into $8832/$8834), scans the keyboard (keys_scan), takes player one's stick from $8821 and player two's from $DC00 into $8EB0/$8EB1, and their direction into $8EB2/$8EB3 ($0F while fire is held, ORed with $B66B/$B66C); then calls $AC96, $931E, $93F9 and $9638 with scroll_dir reset to $0F. $8262 is cleared while either player pushes a direction.
Reads the whole keyboard matrix: each of the eight rows (key_rows) is driven low on CIA 1 port A and its columns read from port B into keys_state ($8821-$8828).
Thirty bytes no traced code reaches: LDA $8821, ORA each of the next seven rows, AND #$1F, STA $8EB1, RTS.
The row-select bytes for keys_scan ($7F to $FE), then the eight single-bit masks $01-$80.
The keyboard matrix as keys_scan last read it, one byte per row (row 7 first, $8821 = the row with SPACE; $8828 = row 0 with F1). The player-one joystick also shows in $8821.
keys_state's byte for keyboard row 6 (right SHIFT among them), the magic test's check against joystick one.
keys_state's byte for keyboard row 1 (the 4 and Z keys), the check against joystick one for player two's magic keys.
keys_state's byte for keyboard row 0: F1, F3, F5, F7, player two's magic keys.
The vertical fine scroll, even values 0-6, ORed into $D011.
The horizontal fine scroll, even values 0-6, ORed into $D016.
Counts the 2-pixel steps of the scroll in progress; at zero the coarse step is done ($8262 raised).
The maze map column at the screen's left edge (0-63).
map_x as it was when the scroll began.
The maze map row at the screen's top (0-63).
map_y as it was when the scroll began.
The direction the screen scrolls in this frame, as joystick bits (active low): $0F is none.
ORed into scroll_dir by scroll_step; cleared each time the players are read.
scroll_dir as the main loop last saw it; the loop skips the slower work on a frame whose direction changed.

Moves the screen 2 pixels in the direction scroll_dir gives: one of eight routines (up, down, left, right and the diagonals) adjusts the fine scrolls, the counters $8266/$8267 and the steps left; when a fine scroll wraps it moves map_x or map_y by one and raises $825F so that the main loop redraws the maze.
Fine scroll X up by 2; when it wraps to 6 the map moves one column (map_x down).
Fine scroll X down by 2; when it wraps to 0 the map moves one column (map_x up).
Both fine scrolls down by 2; at 0 the map moves right and down.
X fine scroll down and Y up; at 0 the map moves right and up (Y from diag_y).
Fine scroll Y up by 2; at 6 the map moves up a row.
Fine scroll Y down by 2; at 0 the map moves down a row.
Both fine scrolls up by 2; at 6 the map moves left and up.
X fine scroll up and Y down; at 6 the map moves left and down (Y from diag_y).
The vertical fine scroll that goes with each horizontal one on a diagonal step: 7 7 5 5 3 3 1 1.

Redraws the maze into the screen behind the one on show and swaps them: works out the map address of the top-left cell ($2000 + map_y x 64 + map_x), rewrites the operands of twenty LDA/STA pairs (one per screen row, offsets from maze_row_ops), and copies 33 columns of 20 rows from the 64 x 64 map to the screen at column 3; the map wraps at its edges through map_wrap_x. Draws into $4000 or $4400 by $FF, flipping it, and sets $8250 so that the raster chain shows the new screen.
The operand of maze_draw's LDY map_wrap_x,X, rewritten with map_x so that the copy starts at the screen's left column.
The low byte of the first row's source in maze_draw's copy loop (the character map at $3000).
The high byte of that source, then the first row's STA.
The second row's source operand, low byte; each row's pair of operands is rewritten by maze_draw through maze_row_ops.
The rest of maze_draw's unrolled copy into the screen at $4000: twenty rows of LDA/STA pairs.
The second half of maze_draw: the same copy into the screen at $4400.
The same column operand in the copy into the screen at $4400.
The first row's source, low byte, for the $4400 copy.
Its high byte.
The second row's source, low byte, for the $4400 copy.
The rest of the unrolled copy into the screen at $4400.
The offset of each row's LDA/STA pair inside the copy loops, $72 down to $00 in sixes; maze_draw rewrites each pair's operands through it.
Waits for the raster interrupt's flag $8264, clears it, then waits until the beam is on the line in A (in the top 256 lines).
Copies the colour of each visible maze cell into colour RAM: the same 33 x 20 window as maze_draw, read from the colour map at $2000 + offset (the operands are set by maze_draw) into $D803 onward.
The column operand in maze_colours' LDY map_wrap_x,X.
The low byte of the first row's source in maze_colours (the colour map at $2000).
The high byte of maze_colours' first source address, in the colour map.
The second row's source operand, low byte.
The rest of maze_colours' unrolled copy into colour RAM: twenty rows.

While the maze font select $8251 is below 8: every eighth call steps $8254 and sets $8251 from panel_font_cycle ($8255: 2 4 2 6), so the maze's characters change font in a four-step cycle; and every fourth frame ($8247) advances the animation step $9124,x (0-3) of each player whose direction bits are not $0F.
Eight bytes no traced code reaches: wait while bit 4 of $DC01 (player one's fire) is high.

Chooses the maze's look from the level header: bits 3-5 of $0A01 pick a 96-byte block of glyphs (from maze_style_src: $6468, $6408 or $6508) copied into the three fonts at $4808, $5008 and $5808; bits 3-5 of $0A02 pick a colour (maze_style_colours) written over $F604-$F643 and $F6CC-$F6D7.
The low byte of maze_style's glyph source, rewritten from maze_style_src.
Its high byte; the rest of maze_style follows.
Six colours for maze_style: $0A $0D $0E $0C $0F $0B.
Five addresses for maze_style's glyph copy: $6468, $6408, $6508, $6408, $6508.
The high bytes of maze_style_src's addresses (read as the second of each pair).

Starts CIA 1's timers as a free-running pair: timer A loaded from the frame counter $8247 (both bytes) and run continuously ($DC0E = $01), timer B counting timer A's underflows ($DC0F = $41); writing $03 to $DC0D turns both timers' interrupts off. Several routines read the timers as a source of random numbers ($AA77, $ADB5, $B1E2, $C4F1, $C970, $C97B, $CBEE).
205 zero bytes before map_wrap_x.
0 to 63 then 0 to 47: a map column plus an offset, wrapped to the map's width, for maze_draw, maze_colours and the routines that look up map cells.
map_wrap_x read one column on.
map_wrap_x read two columns on.

Adds a transporter to the list of those on screen: its map cell ($B29A, $B29B) times four, kept below $80, into teleport_x/teleport_y at the next free slot (teleport_count, which it increments). Called from $B1CC.

Sends player X ($910D) through a transporter. A stick held still, or a direction whose facing (facing_of_dir) is odd, returns 1 and does nothing; otherwise the point eight units ahead of the player in the pushed direction (dir_dx/dir_dy) is the aim, which is how the stick steers the jump. With fewer than two transporters on screen it returns 2. Otherwise it measures each transporter's distance from the aim (the sum of the two differences, through $BFAB), sorts the list nearest first (teleport_sort), and tries them in order (teleport_place), returning 3 if none had room.
Bubble-sorts the transporter list by distance (teleport_dist), keeping each entry's X and Y with it; two at the same distance are swapped when bit 0 of $B92F,x is set, which breaks ties by chance.

Tries the sorted transporters from the list's second entry on, skipping any at distance 0, and for each tries the eight cells around it, starting from the player's facing (teleport_free): the first free one gets the player. The player's map position is moved there (the old cells cleared and the new marked, through cell_addr), the pointer pair $C0/$C1 + 2X set from $8E/$8F, and sound $0B started ($CDDB).
