Plays one frame of the tune when tune_on is set: for each of the three voices counts its note down ($A046, $A050, $A05A, with a second byte for long notes) and, when it runs out, reads the voice's next commands (tune_command) with $82/$83 at its state and $84 at its SID registers (0, 7, $0E).

Reads one two-byte command from the voice's stream at ($80) and acts on it. A first byte with bit 7 set is a note: its number less $80 picks the frequency (note_freqs), the second byte is its length in frames, and the gate is cleared and set again from the voice's control byte. 0: a rest of the given length, the gate cleared. 1: volume and filter ($D418). 2, 3, 4, $0A: the value goes to the voice's register 5 (attack/decay), its control byte (kept, and written to register 4), register 3 (pulse width high) or register 6 (sustain/release). $19: a long rest, the value less one into the high count byte. $1E: the end, every gate off and tune_on cleared. $11: marks a loop start. $10: loops back to the mark the given number of times. $1B: adds the value to the volume. Commands that set a register go straight on to the next; a note or a rest ends the voice's work for the frame.
An RTS byte no code reaches.
tune_command's common tail for the commands that set a register: writes the value, steps on and reads the next command.
A second RTS byte, after tune_reg_write, that no code reaches.
Plays a note: sets the voice's frequency from note_freqs, keeps its length, clears the gate and then writes the control byte.
Steps the stream pointer $80/$81 past one two-byte command.
The tune player's note table: 96 SID frequencies, two bytes each (low first), from $010C up a semitone a step.
note_freqs read from its second byte (the high bytes).

For a level that has a hidden potion (hidden_kind 0-5 but not 4): copies its 16-byte graphic from $6580 + 16 x kind into the three maze fonts at $4970, $5170 and $5970, turns the kind into its tile ($19 + kind) and puts it in a random free place (random_place).
The low byte of hidden_potion_place's LDA $6580,Y, rewritten with the potion's 16-byte block.

From level 8 on (and not in a treasure room): puts a random 1 to N extra objects in random free places, N being 4 for levels 8-31, 8 for 32-63, 12 for 64-95 and 16 from 96 (bits 2-3 of level_number / 8, plus 4). Each is tile $14, or $15 when the count left is a multiple of four, or $31 when a random byte is below extras_chance ($19, about one in ten).
The most extra objects extras_place puts in this level.
$19: the random number below which an extra object is $31.

Puts the object in hidden_kind somewhere free: picks random cell positions ($BE6E, $BE6F) until the place is free ($BDBF, $BE1A), flashing the border while it looks, then draws the object's characters and colours into the maps from tile_chars (via $CAD3 and $CB42) and writes the object into the tile grid.
The object being placed: the hidden potion's kind (0-5), or the tile of an extra object; $FF for none.

A random byte in A: an additive generator over the four zero-page bytes $26-$29, each having the previous byte's old value added with the carry (the first gets $29), returning $26. Seeded from the raster line when a player joins (wait_first_player).

At the start of a level from file 8 on: a random 0-15 into hidden_kind; below 6, the level gets a hidden potion of that kind and "FIND THE HIDDEN POTION" is printed. The placing routine skips kind 4, which keeps the message.
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): str_hidden_potion at $A47A, "FIND THE HIDDEN POTION".
hidden_potion_roll's return.
"FIND THE HIDDEN POTION", length $16, colour 1.

Raises $B65F and runs $B9D0; when no player is in the game and both leave timers have run out, drops the main loop's return address and goes back to the start-up's wait for players (j_8091): the game is over.

Clears what a new game starts without: the border, both players' $B663-$B666 and $B66D/$B66E, the four shot slots, both players' states, the counters $B929-$B930 and $B65A, and the players' position bytes ($9100-$9107); sets $B65B to $1E, $B931/$B932 to $20 and both freeze masks ($B66B/$B66C) to $0F.

The start of a game: draws the empty panels and their colours, then waits until a fire button is pressed (stick_p1/stick_p2), seeds the random generator from the raster line, puts that player in the game at the start tile (player_join), sets its powers (player_powers_reset) and marks its cells.
During play, a player not in the game who presses fire joins (join_beside), as long as somebody is playing.

Puts player X in beside the other player: tries the four places next to it (join_spot); with none free, plays sound $0D and leaves; otherwise places X there, links the two (player_other), marks its cells, redraws the panel and clears both freeze masks.
Tries the four places next to the other player, above, left, below and right (join_offsets, y = 3 down to 0): carry clear for the first free one, its position in $B29A/$B29B.
Looks at the tile grid beside the other player in direction Y; carry clear when that tile is 0.
Five bytes read as overlapping pairs, Y offset from $A624,y and X from $A625,y: y = 3 above ($F8, 0), 2 left (0, $F8), 1 below (8, 0), 0 right (0, 8).
join_offsets read as X offsets.
Marks player X's four character cells occupied.

For each player not in the game with its leave timer running: raises $B65F, zeroes the panel's health ($B92F, $B931) and puts glyph $10 over its digits; when the timer runs out, resets the player's counters, health $B931 to $20 and powers, and puts "PRESS FIRE" in its panel.

Code and text no traced code reaches: prints "INSERT SIDE 2 OF DISK", "THEN PRESS SPACE BAR", "TO CONTINUE GAME", clears bit 5 of $01 (the cassette motor line), waits for $DC01 bit 4 to be pressed and released, sets the bit again and redraws. A leftover of a two-sided release; the strings are at $A6CE, $A6E5 and $A6FB.
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): unused_side2 + 59 at $A6CE, "INSERT SIDE 2 OF DISK".
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): unused_side2 + 82 at $A6E5, "THEN PRESS SPACE BAR".
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): unused_side2 + 104 at $A6FB, "TO CONTINUE GAME".
The rest of unused_side2's code: clears bit 5 of $01, waits for $DC01 bit 4 to be pressed and released, sets the bit again, clears the screen and waits; no traced code reaches it.
"INSERT SIDE 2 OF DISK".
"THEN PRESS SPACE BAR".
"TO CONTINUE GAME".
Fires the players' shots: shot slots 3 and 2 (player two's and player one's) through shot_fire.

Fires shot slot X (2 or 3, the player X - 2) when the slot is free, the player is in the game with a state below 4, and its fire bit is pressed (stick_p1/p2 below $10): the shot's direction is the stick's facing, or the walking step when the stick is centred, its sprite shape the direction plus the hero's base ($A878,x), its position the player's; the slot is set to the hero's shot type + 1 ($911A,x + 1), the sprite placed (shot_sprite), sound 4 started, and $B65B reloaded from $B65C.

Moves the four shot slots each frame: a slot holding 6 goes to $A7BF; others step along their direction (X by $BE80,y at $A7A1, Y by $BE70,y at $A7AB, the index raised by shot_speed $ACC2,x for a fast shot), with the shape turning every fourth frame for type 1, and their sprite is placed again; a slot with bit 7 set goes to $A92E.

Moves a lobbed rock (shot type 6) every fourth frame: steps its position by its per-step offsets ($ABEB, $ABED), counts its steps down ($ABE7) and ends it at zero (shot_clear); in the first half of the flight it rises (Y up two units a step, its shape stepping towards $AF), in the second it falls (Y down two units, the shape $AD-$AF by height).

Places shot slot X's sprite from its maze position: X on screen = (shot X - scroll) x 2 + $38 with the high bit, Y = (shot Y - scroll) x 2 + $37. A shot off the left of the screen or below row $50 is ended instead.
Each of the four shot slots' contents: 0 empty; 1-4 a player's shot (the hero + 1; slots 2 and 3); 5 a monster's fireball and 6 a lobbed rock (slots 0 and 1); bit 7 set ends it.
Shot slot 1's contents.
Shot slot 2's contents (player one's shot).
Shot slot 3's contents (player two's shot).
Each shot's direction (0-7).
Each shot's maze X.
Each shot's maze Y.

For a monster's shot (slots 0 and 1), the monster's slot in the monster table; $A866/$A867 are $FF for the players' slots. Then sixteen bytes no traced code reads by name, a pattern of direction steps: 0 4 4 4 0 $FC $FC $FC $FC $FC 0 4 4 4 0 $FC.
The first sprite shape of each slot's shots: $B8, $B8 (monsters), $D8, $F8 (players: within each player's block of shapes).
How the Warrior's thrown axe turns every fourth frame, by direction: -1 or +1 to its shape.
For each shot in flight (not a rock): works out its tile and its 4-unit cell ($A93D, $A941) and what the shot does to the tile there (shot_tile).

What a shot does to the tile it reaches. Floor: nothing. Tiles $14 (the jug) and $16 (the blue potion), the special potions $19-$1E and the jug $31 are destroyed with the shot ($AD30, the tile cleared, $B4EA). Walls, doors, the chest, $15, $17 and $32 stop the shot. $18, $1F, $2F, $30 and the exit $36 let it fly on. A generator ($20-$2E) loses the shot's power ($ACAB,x) from its value; below the threshold for its kind ($ACAF) it is destroyed ($AC17 scores, then as above); otherwise it is redrawn ($B517) and a player's shot scores ($AC17). A crumbling wall ($33-$35) moves one stage on, and the stage after $35 is cleared away.
Empties shot slot X and hides its sprite.
Each shot's X in 4-unit cells, for the monster test.
Each shot's Y in cells.

Tests monster Y (unless bit 3 of its flags, $0640, is set) against every shot in flight but its own and a rock still rising: a shot within one cell either way hits it and ends. A monster with strength ($0580) $C0 or more, Death, is not hurt: a player's shot adds 1 to the low byte of the score (decimal) and shows it ($AD16). Otherwise the strength drops by the shot's power ($ACBE,x) and the shot scores (shot_score); a monster left with less than nothing is taken off the map ($BDBF, $C35A with its position) and out of the table, the last monster moving into its slot and the count ($824E) going down; carry set.
Work: the tested monster's X / 2.
Work: the tested monster's Y / 2.
Runs shot_hits_monster for every monster in the table (0 to $824E, while it has any), not stepping on after a removal.

A demon (monster Y) shoots: with slot 1 or 0 free, puts a fireball (type 5) in it at the demon's place, heading the demon's facing (its strength's low three bits), shape $B8 + the direction, colour 7; marks the demon as having shot (bit 5 of its flags).

A lobber (monster $824A) throws a rock about one time in eight (CIA 1 timer A's low bits): when the rock's path to its target works out (rock_path), a rock (type 6, shape $AD, colour 7) starts at the lobber, which is marked as having thrown (bit 5 of its flags), and sound $0C plays.
The colour of sprites 2-5: the shots in slots 0-3, and the level digits.
Slot 1's colour.
Slot 2's colour.
Slot 3's colour.
For each player and each shot in flight that is not the player's own: a shot in the same 8-unit square as the player hits it ($AC3E) and ends.

Works out a lobbed rock's flight for slot X from its distance to the target ($BF83, $BF85): the longer axis decides the number of steps (1-7, at most 15 for the height count), the step on each axis in two-unit moves with the signs put back, and the half-way count for the arc; carry set when both monster slots are busy or the target is too far.

rock_path's work bytes: the two distances with their signs ($ABE1-$ABE6), the step count and its half for each slot ($ABE7, $ABE9), the per-step X and Y moves ($ABEB, $ABED), and whether the axes were swapped ($ABEF).
rock_path's X distance, halved.
rock_path's Y distance, signed.
The Y distance, halved.
The longer of the two, doubled.
The shorter, doubled.
Each rock slot's steps left.
Each rock slot's half-way step.
Each rock slot's X move per step.
Each rock slot's Y move per step.
Set when the X and Y axes were swapped.

Adds 5 (decimal) to the score of the player whose shot slot X is (2 or 3; monsters' shots score nothing), carrying through the three score bytes ($B929/$B92B/$B92D, $B92A/$B92C/$B92E), and raises $B65F to redraw the panel.
Adds 10 (decimal) to the score of the player whose shot or blow slot X is (2 or 3; nothing for X below 2), carrying through the score bytes, and raises $B65F to redraw the panel.

What a shot does to player Y it hits. A fireball (type 5) takes 10 health and a rock (type 6) 3, subtracted in decimal from the player's health ($B92F/$B931). A player's shot: on a level whose header sets bit 1 ("shots now stun") the player is frozen ($911E,y = 5); with bit 0 ("shots now hurt") it loses the shot's damage ($ACBE,x) / 4. A player whose health goes below zero gets $C40C,x raised. Raises $B65F and plays sound 8.
While a player's leave timer ($911E,x) runs, its stick reads as nothing pressed and its direction as none.
The power of a shot against generators, by shot slot: slots 0 and 1 (monsters' shots) 1; slots 2 and 3 are the players' ($ACAD).
Each player's shot power against generators (shot slots 2 and 3), set by hero and by the shot-power potion.

For each generator tile ($20-$2E, three per kind, the strongest last), the value below which a hit destroys it: $20 $20 $20 $23 $23 $23 ... $2C $2C $2C. A hit lowers the tile's value, so a strong generator is first knocked down to a weaker one.
A shot's damage to monsters by shot slot: $40 for the monsters' slots 0 and 1; slots 2 and 3 are the players' ($ACC0).
Each player's shot damage to monsters, set by hero and by the shot-power potion.
A shot's speed by slot, added to its direction to pick its step from $BE70/$BE80: 0 for slots 0 and 1; slots 2 and 3 are the players' ($ACC4).
Each player's shot speed: 0, or 8 with the shot-speed potion; then two bytes of 1.
Each player's hand-to-hand power against generators.
Hand-to-hand damage to monsters by slot ($40, $40); the players' are at $ACCC.
Each player's hand-to-hand damage, set by hero and by the fight-power potion.

A player pushing into a generator (tile in A, $20-$2E) fights it: on every fourth call (fight_rate), the generator's value drops by the player's fight power ($ACC8); below its threshold it is cleared. Either way it is redrawn ($B517) and the player scores (score_generator).
The countdown fight_generator uses per player, from 4.
After a hit on Death, takes the next value of death_scores (cycling through eight) into $AD27, which $C489 reads.
Counts Death hits, for death_points.
The value death_points last chose.
Eight values death_points cycles through: $40 $80 $60 $50 $70 $30 $20 $10.
A shot destroyed tile A: for tile $16 or $18-$1E it sets $BACD, which sets off a potion's effect ($BACE), and plays sound 5.

A potion's blast on the generator at ($8E),y (kind in A): its value drops by the player's magic ($A00A,x); below the threshold it is destroyed (scored, cleared, $B4EA), otherwise redrawn ($B517) and scored.
In a treasure room, every twelfth call takes a second off the clock ($ADB4) and the units digit sprite ($9157, shapes $A2-$AB) down by one, the tens digit ($9156) too when the units pass 0.
Counts the calls to treasure_clock between seconds, from $0B.
The seconds left in a treasure room; at zero the room ends (the main loop's test at $815A).
Picks a treasure room's time at random (CIA 1 timer A's low bits): from treasure_times, 20 to 30 seconds, with the two digit sprites to match.
The units digit's sprite shape for each of the sixteen random times.
The tens digit's shape.

The end of a treasure room: plays sound $10 and waits for it (sfx_wait), clears the takings of a player who did not escape ($AF38/$AF3A), clears the screen, prints each player's result (treasure_result), turns the tune player off (tune_on, tune_wanted $8249 and treasure_tune_due $B0FE cleared) and rewinds the treasure tune at $E800 (tune_init, which leaves it off until treasure_start turns it on), runs $CD77 and waits.

Prints player X's result in its hero colour: with nothing collected, "NO BONUS" and "LOOKS LIKE YOU LOSE!"; otherwise "TREASURES nn" and "BONUS nn00", the count ($AF3A) added in decimal to the score's middle byte, a hundred points a treasure.
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): str_treasures + 30 at $AF18, "NO BONUS".
treasure_result goes on after "NO BONUS": "LOOKS LIKE YOU LOSE!" and the rows below.
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): str_treasures + 40 at $AF22, "LOOKS LIKE YOU LOSE!".
treasure_result's rows after its strings.

Part of treasure_result: turns the treasure count's digits into one decimal byte and adds it to the score. Its address is also where pinn232 calls the BASIC ROM ($AE86), which the snapshot shows as this RAM beneath.
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): str_treasures at $AEFA, "TREASURES" and the count.
treasure_result goes on after "TREASURES nn": the BONUS line.
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): the BONUS line at $AF0A, "BONUS" and the bonus.
treasure_result's last rows.
The address of each hero's name for the message screens.
The high bytes of hero_name_ptrs.
The four heroes' names for the message screens, each a length, a colour and the glyphs: WARRIOR ($90-$97), VALKYRIE, WIZARD, ELF ($5B-$5E).
"VALKYRIE" for the message screens.
"WIZARD".
"ELF", in the panel font's own glyphs.
"TREASURES " and two digits ($AF08/$AF09), then "BONUS " and digits ($AF14), "NO BONUS" ($AF18) and "LOOKS LIKE YOU LOSE!" ($AF22): each a length, a colour and the text.
The TREASURES line's colour byte, set to the hero's colour.
The count's tens digit.
The count's units digit.
The BONUS line: length and colour.
Its colour byte, set to the hero's colour, then "BONUS".
The bonus's first digit.
The bonus's second digit, then "00".
"NO BONUS": length and colour.
Its colour byte, then the text.
"LOOKS LIKE YOU LOSE!": length and colour.
The colour byte of "LOOKS LIKE YOU LOSE!", set to the hero's colour, then its text.
Set for a player who leaves a treasure room through its exit, from the time left ($ADB4).
Player two's escape flag.
The treasures each player picked up in a treasure room.
Player two's treasures.
Levels left before the next treasure room (level_pick).
The rows text_row can choose for the message screens, colour RAM then screen: X = 0 colour $D918 and screen $4118, X = 2 colour $D878 and screen $4078.
The colour row addresses' high bytes.
The screen row addresses, low byte first.
Their high bytes.
Sets the frame counter $8247 to $C0 and waits until it comes round to zero: 64 frames.
Puts sprites 2-4 at X and Y 0.
Puts the scroll back to its rest position (fine Y 7, X 0), hides the digit sprites, then text_screen.

Turns the screen over to text: freezes both players, empties the four shot slots, hides sprites 4-7, colours sprites 2-5 blue (6), waits for the scrolling to stop, clears the screen at $4000 and its colour, shows it with no sprites, and sets the panel font (font select 8, $C60A).
Picks the message screen's first row by the number of players in the game (two players start higher), then text_row.
Points $8C/$8D at a row of the message screen and $8E/$8F at its colour (text_rows, entry X).

Prints a string centred on the row at $8C/$8D (colour at $8E/$8F). The string's address is the two bytes after the JSR, which this routine skips on return. A string is a length, a colour and the characters; each character is written less $20 (the font's own order) and its colour beside it; the row pointers then move down a row (text_next_row).
Moves the text row pointers $8C/$8D and $8E/$8F down one row (40 bytes).
The colour print_centred is writing in.
Turns the number in A (0-255) into three ASCII digits: hundreds in X, tens in Y, units in A.

The start of a treasure room: clears the screen, prints "YOU HAVE FOUND A" and the two rows of big letters "TREASURE ROOM", sets the clock (treasure_clock_set), prints the level's messages and asks for the treasure tune (treasure_tune_due).
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): str_treasure_room at $B0FF, "YOU HAVE FOUND A".
treasure_intro goes on after its first string: the big letters.
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): the top half of the big TREASURE ROOM at $B111.
After the top half of the big letters: the bottom half.
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): the bottom half of the big TREASURE ROOM at $B12D.
After the strings: the clock, the messages and the tune flag.
On the first pass of a treasure room: starts the tune at $E800 with the tune player (tune_start), runs $CD77, turns the tune on, and puts the clock's two digit sprites at X $A8 and $BC, Y $36.
Set by treasure_intro; treasure_start clears it once it has started the tune.

"YOU HAVE FOUND A" ($10 long, colour 1), then the big "TREASURE ROOM" in two rows of the font's large-letter glyphs ($E3-$F4 for the top halves at $B111, $03-$14 for the bottom at $B12D), $1A long, colour $0E.
The top half of the big "TREASURE ROOM".
The bottom half.
Moves the text row pointers down X + 1 rows.
Prints player X's hero's name (from hero_name_ptrs, by writing the address into its own call's argument at $B164) and moves down a row.
print_hero_name's argument: the address of the hero's name, rewritten from hero_name_ptrs before the call.
The high byte of print_hero_name's argument.
print_hero_name goes on after its string: next row and return.

Every eighth pass (while somebody plays, or at once while a potion's blast is under way, $BACD), with fewer than 192 monsters: looks at the 16 x 10 tiles on screen (from map_x / 2, map_y / 2). A transporter ($30) is added to the list (teleport_add). A generator ($20-$2E) is hit by the blast if there is one (magic_generator), and picks a random direction (the CIA 1 timers mixed): if the cell that way is free (gen_spot), a monster of its kind comes out there (monster_spawn).
Works out the cell beside the generator in direction X (gen_dx, gen_dy) as a position in $BE6E/$BE6F and asks whether it is free ($BDBF, $BE1A).

Adds a monster to the table (unless it holds 192): its position from the generator's tile and the direction, its kind byte (monster_kinds for the generator's tile, ORed with the direction as its facing) in $0580, its flags cleared; then marks it in the maps ($BDDE) and draws it ($CAD3, $CB42).
The monster byte for each generator tile $20-$2E: the level in bits 6-7 ($00, $40, $80) and the kind in bits 3-5, so three tiles to a kind: ghosts $20-$22, then four more kinds.
The X step for each of the eight directions: 0 1 1 1 0 -1 -1 -1.
The generator being run, its tile less $20.
The tile column being looked at (generators_run, teleport_add, join_beside).
The tile row being looked at.
generators_run's column counter.
generators_run's row counter.
A zero byte after the generator scan's counters.

A trap's effect: goes through the whole tile grid ($0C00-$0FFF), clearing every trap tile ($2F) and every tile with bit 7 set (the walls a trap takes away), each with its neighbours' brick joins put right (trap_wall_gone), and blanking their cells (cell_blank).

Removes the wall at ($8C) whose low bits say which sides it joins (bit 0 above, 1 right, 2 below, 3 left): the wall on each of those sides has the matching join taken out of its shape (wall_unjoin), then the tile is cleared and its cells blanked.
Takes the join Y (wall_join_masks) out of the wall tile at ($8E), if it is a plain wall ($01-$0F); a wall left with no joins becomes $10; then redraws it (tile_draw).
The masks wall_unjoin uses for the four sides: $0B $07 $0E $0D.
Runs the two door-opening processes (door_state $B4E7 and $B4E9, here as X 0 and 2), one step each per pass. A key starts both from the same door (door_unlock), spreading in different directions.

One step of a door opening: the state (8-11) says which way the opening is spreading; the door tile next to it that way (or across) is cleared and drawn as floor (door_clear), and the process moves on to it; with no door left that way it turns or stops. Bit 7 alternates the two directions it tries.
Points $8E/$8F at the tile left of the door process's tile ($B4E3).
Points $8E/$8F at the tile to the right.
Points $8E/$8F at the tile above, wrapping within the grid.
Points $8E/$8F at the tile below.
Clears the tile at ($8E) (writes Y, 0), makes it the process's position and blanks its four character cells ($C369).
Zero flag set when the tile at ($8E) is a door ($11 or $12).
The tile address each door process has reached (two bytes for each).
The first door process's tile address, high byte.
The second door process's tile address.
The high byte of the second door process's tile address.
The first door process: 0 none, 8-11 the direction it is spreading in, bit 7 which of two it tries next.
The second door process.
Writes zero into the four character map cells of the tile at ($8C) in the tile grid: the tile's graphics are gone.
Draws tile A at tile grid address ($8E) into the character map: its four characters from tile_chars ($F400 + tile x 4).

Every twelfth pass (a game second) counts down $B65B. In stage 0, when it runs out, the doors open (idle_doors_open). In stage 1, after the next count, every wall becomes an exit (idle_walls_exit). A player firing puts the count back ($A75E), so it measures time without shooting.
The first stage: tiles from $11 to $12 (the doors) and every key become floor; plays sound $0E.
The second stage: tiles from $01 to $10 (the walls), the crumbling walls $33-$35 and the keys become exits ($36); plays sound $10.
Replaces every tile in the grid in the range idle_lo to idle_hi less one, and every key, by idle_new, and draws each one (tile_redraw); when idle_new is not zero the crumbling walls too.
Draws tile A at grid position Y of the page at $8F into the character map ($3000) and the colour map ($2000), characters from $F400 and colours from $F600 + tile x 4.
The lowest tile tiles_replace replaces.
One above the highest.
What it puts in their place.
The idle timer's stage: 0, 1, then 2 when both have happened.
The idle timer's count, in game seconds.
The count a shot puts back ($1E, 30 seconds).
The count for the second stage ($96, 150).
Raised by anything that changes what the panel shows; the panel is redrawn while it is non-zero.
The tile below which tile_blocks treats a tile as a wall: $13, or $11 for a player with keys.
Set when the player's keys and potions together reach the carrying limit: tile_blocks then lets keys and potions block the way like walls.
The tile the player is picking up.
The keys each player carries.
Player two's keys.
The potions each player carries.
Player two's potions.
Each player's limit of keys and potions together: 10, 15 with the carrying potion.
Each player's amulet countdown: set to $FF when it picks one up (amulet_take); while it runs the player's sprite flashes and its state is 3 (amulet_flash).
ORed into player one's direction: $0F holds the player still (message screens, traps), 0 lets it move.
Player two's.

A joystick direction that overrides the stick's for each player, a direction code as the stick gives it (not a facing 0-7): exit_spin stores its spin_facings values here ($BAE3, from $BB26), and players_sprites reads it at $917A in place of the stick and turns it into a facing through facing_of_dir.
Player two's facing override.
Set to $30 for a player who steps into an exit ($B784); read by $BAD7.

Notes what player X is about to touch: of the eight tiles around it (pointers $B0-$BF), the one in the direction it pushes, if it is $11 or above, or $2F, $31 or $36; the tile goes into player_under and level_name,y, and its grid address into $C0/$C1 + 2X (touch_note).
Copies the grid address of neighbour X into the player's $C0/$C1 pair.

For each player in the game, acts on the tile it touched: a transporter ($30) goes to teleport_try, a generator ($20-$2E) to fight_generator, the exit ($36) to pickup_take; anything else (below $20, or $2F and above) is cleared from the grid and goes to pickup_take.
Uses the transporter when the player is in the game and pushed into it this pass (player_moved).

Picks up the tile in tile_touched for player X/2. The exit ($36) takes the player out of the level (exit_enter); otherwise the tile's cells are blanked and: a trap ($2F) springs (trap_set); the jug $31 is poison (poison_eaten); anything else from $11 runs the routine pickup_routines gives for it (its JMP at $B767 rewritten) after the sound pickup_sounds gives.
The JMP rewritten by pickup_take with the pickup's routine.
The low byte of pickup_jump's JMP, rewritten with the pickup's routine.
The high byte of pickup_jump's target.

Player X steps into an exit: its state gets bit 7 (leaving), its escape time is noted ($AF38 = treasure_time), it is frozen, exit_count set to $30 for the spin into the exit, $824C cleared and sound 6 started.
A trap: sets trap_pending, freezes both players and plays sound $10; the trap springs (trap_spring) when both sticks are let go (trap_wait).
The poison: clears the screen, prints the hero's name, "HAS JUST EATEN SOME" and "POISONED FOOD!", applies the poison (poison), plays sound $10, waits and puts the maze back.
poison_eaten's first argument: the address of the hero's name, rewritten from hero_name_ptrs before the call.
The high byte of poison_eaten's first argument, the hero's name.
poison_eaten goes on after the hero's name: "HAS JUST EATEN SOME".
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): str_poisoned at $B7E5, "HAS JUST EATEN SOME".
After it: "POISONED FOOD!".
The address of the string the call before prints (print_centred's argument): str_poisoned + 21 at $B7FA, "POISONED FOOD".
After the strings: the poison's effect, the sound, the wait and the maze.
"HAS JUST EATEN SOME" ($13 long, colour 1) and "POISONED FOOD!" ($0D, at $B7FA).
"POISONED FOOD!".
Runs exit_spin for both players.
When a trap is pending and neither player pushes a direction: springs it (trap_spring), lets both players move again and clears the trap.
Set by trap_set until the trap springs.

The routine for each pickup tile from $11: doors $11 and $12 (door_unlock), chest $13 (chest_take), food $14 and $15 (food_eat), potions $16 and $17 (potion_take), the amulet $18 (amulet_take), the six special potions $19-$1E, the key $1F (key_take).
pickup_routines read from its second byte.
The sound each pickup tile from $11 plays: $0E for the doors, $11 for most, 9 for the amulet, 7 for the key.
Opens a door with a key: starts both door processes from it, spreading in two directions (door_state $89 and $8B), takes a key and its icon from the panel, and scores 100 (score_100).
Adds 1 to the middle byte of player X's score in decimal (100 points), carrying into the high byte, and raises panel_dirty.
Food: adds 100 to player X's health (in decimal, to the hundreds byte $B931) and scores 100.
A potion: draws its icon (glyph 4) in the panel, counting down from the block's right ($832F,x less the potions held), adds it to potions_held and scores 100.
The amulet: sets the amulet countdown to $FF and the player's state to 3, and scores 100.
24 bytes no traced code reaches: the same as potion_take but for the colour row ($DB98 in place of $DB9C).
A key: draws its icon (glyph 3, colour 7) in the panel, adds it to keys_held and scores 100.
Takes one potion from player X and wipes its icon from the panel.
A treasure chest: counts it for the treasure room (treasures_got) and, on an ordinary level, scores 100.
The last two bytes of chest_take (its JMP's high byte and RTS), which the score routines name as a base: indexed with a shot slot (2 or 3), $B927 + X is score_lo.
The low byte of each player's score in decimal ($B929, $B92A); the middle bytes are at $B92B, the high at $B92D.
Player two's low score byte.
Player one's middle score byte (hundreds and thousands).
Player two's middle score byte (hundreds and thousands).
Player one's high score byte.
Player two's high score byte.
The low byte of each player's health, in decimal ($B92F, $B930): the tens and units.
Player two's health, tens and units, in decimal.
The high byte of each player's health in decimal, the thousands and hundreds: $20 is 2000.
Player two's health, thousands and hundreds, in decimal.

For each player in the game and not leaving: counts its freeze timer ($911E,x) down and takes one from its health in decimal; a player whose health goes below zero gets $C40C,x raised, its health set to zero, and leaves the game (player_leaves). Raises panel_dirty and counts magic_debounce down. The raster interrupt calls it every 64th frame, and every frame while $C40C/$C40D is set.
Takes out of the game each player whose $C40C,x is set (its health zeroed, player_leaves).

For each player: one that has left the level (bit 6) has its sprite turned off; one with the amulet's countdown running has its sprite toggled every pass (the flicker of invisibility) and, when the countdown ends, its sprite back on and its state back to 1.
When panel_dirty is set: clears it and redraws both players' score and health digits (panel_digits).
Writes player X's score (six digits from $B92D, $B92B, $B929) and health (four from $B931, $B92F) into the panel's third row, each digit as glyph $10 + its value.
Stops a held magic key from using a second potion: set to 2 when one is used, counted down by health_tick.

Reads the magic keys. Player one's is SPACE: its bit low in keyboard row 7 ($8821) but not in row 6 ($8822), which tells it from joystick one's fire button (low in every row). Player two's is any of F1, F3, F5, F7 (row 0, $8828) with row 1's bits 3 and 4 ($8827) high, the same test against the joystick. A player in the game and not leaving uses a potion (magic_use).
Uses one of player X's potions when no blast is under way: starts the blast (blast_owner = X + 3), takes the potion (potion_drop), and plays sound 5; with no potion, sound $0D.

Non-zero while a potion's blast is under way: 1 for a shot potion, 3 or 4 for player one's or two's (the player + 3); the blast hits the generators (generators_run) and the monsters on screen (monsters_run).

The spin of player X into an exit, while its state has bit 7 and not bit 6: the facing steps round (spin_facings) as exit_count runs down; at $0F the shapes switch to a smaller set ($18 on), and when the count is done the shapes go back, the state gets bit 6 (left the level), the sprite goes off and the players are unlinked.
The facings a player turns through going into an exit.

Moves the monsters on screen. With a potion's blast under way it goes to blast_hit. Otherwise, on three passes in four (bits 1-2 of $824B not both clear), it works through up to half the table from where it stopped last time ($BE6D), moving each monster that is on screen (monster_step), and stops early when the raster interrupt asks the main loop to redraw ($8264) or there are 192 monsters.
How many monsters monsters_run may still move this pass.
Moves monster Y if it is on screen ($BD06); steps Y on by one, or by two when the monster was removed.
A potion's blast: flashes the maze's second colour white ($D022), hits every monster on screen ($C429), clears blast_owner and puts the colour back ($0B).
Carry clear when monster Y's position is within the 34 x 22 cells of the screen (map_x/map_y less one).
A SEC byte between monster_on_screen's two returns that no code reaches.
monster_on_screen's return with the carry set (off screen).

Monster Y next to player X attacks. Except for a ghost, a monster whose chosen facing is odd (monster_facings) does not. A monster on the player's very spot is removed (monster_remove); one more than four cells off on either axis does nothing. A ghost does not attack from a diagonal (ghost_diagonal). Then monster_hits ($C3AC) takes the health on alternate attempts and lets the player hit back; carry set from it means the player's blow killed the monster, and the routine returns. A ghost hits once and vanishes (taken off the map, $C584, and out of the table, sound 0); Death (kind 5) takes 4 health a touch (in decimal) while its drain count ($0700,y) lasts, the player leaving the game if its health runs out, and is removed when the count is used up; the other kinds play sound $0A. Carry set when the monster was removed.
Part of monster_attack: Death's touch, 4 health off in decimal and the player out of the game when it runs out. Its address is also where pinn232 calls the BASIC ROM ($BC9B).
Takes monster Y out of the table: the last monster moves into its slot and the count goes down.
Carry clear when the player is exactly four cells off on both axes, diagonally next to the monster.

Moves monster Y one step. Its old cells are cleared from the maps ($BDBF, $C35A); it picks a direction towards its target (monster_aim, which also runs the attack); with bit 0 of the result set and no attack it tries another way (monster_turn). Unless an attack happened, it looks one step along its facing (monster_next): if the cells there are free (monster_cells_free) it goes there, a sorcerer (kind 4) changing its visibility as it goes (bit 3 of its flags, with a count in bits 6-7); otherwise it stays and only turns. The monster is drawn where it ends up (character and colour, $CA7F/$CB5D, or $CBB1 for a sorcerer out of sight) and may shoot ($C49E).
Ten bytes no traced code reaches: clear bit 5 of monster Y's flags and return with carry clear.
From the cell position in $BE6E/$BE6F, points $F7/$F8 at its colour map byte ($2000 page) and $F9/$FA at its character map byte ($3000 page).
Points $FB and $FD at monster Y's tile graphics: its tile is $40 + its kind and facing ($0580 & $3F), four bytes each in tile_chars and the colour table.
The cell monster Y's facing leads to: its position plus one step (mon_dx/mon_dy) into $BE6E/$BE6F, kept even.
Zero when the monster's two-by-two cells at the new position are all empty and no attack has happened ($BFF1); at the map's right or bottom edge ($7E) it reads the wrapped cells.
Zero when the four character cells at ($F9) are all zero and $BFF1 is clear.
Where monsters_run starts next time.
A cell position being looked at (X), in the units of the monster table.
The Y of that position.
The Y step for each facing, two cells for monsters ($BE70-$BE77), three for fast shots ($BE78-$BE7F).
The X step for each facing, two cells and three.

Aims monster Y: measures each target player's distance (in X, in Y, and the two added; a player leaving or under the amulet is ignored), picks the nearer (monster_target), and makes a facing towards it from the signs. A lobber (kind 3) nearer than $18 turns the other way, so lobbers keep their distance. Then the attack is tried (monster_attack); when it removed the monster, the caller's return is dropped.
Picks which player monsters go for: the nearer when both are in the game, otherwise the one that is.
The target player for each combination of players in the game.
Set when player two is the nearer.
The player being aimed at.
For each player, the monster's X distance from it, signed.
The Y distance.
For each player, the two distances added.
The monster's distance from player two, the two axes added.
The direction the monster wants, as stick bits.
4 when the monster runs away (its facing flipped), 0 otherwise.
The stick value for each of the sixteen direction-bit combinations a monster can want.
The facing for each combination.
The facing monster_aim chose.
Folds a difference on the 128-unit maze into -64 to 63, so that distances work across the edges of a maze that wraps.

A blocked monster tries another way: one of four routines (turn_routines, picked by the facing) is called through the JSR at $BFD1, whose operand is rewritten; the facing chosen from the result goes into the monster's byte.
The JSR monster_turn rewrites with one of turn_routines.
The low byte of turn_call's target.
Its target, high byte; then monster_turn's tail, which turns the routine's answer into a facing.
Set when a monster has attacked this step (blocks its move).
The four turning routines: $C105, $C27E, $C1C4, $C043.
turn_routines read from its second byte.
Six bytes after the turning routines' table: 0 0 1 8 0 0.
Fourteen bytes before monsters_draw_all that no traced code reads by address: 8 2 0 0 2 4 0 0 4 1 0 0 $FF 1.
Draws every monster in the table into the maps at the start of a level: for each, its tile graphics (monster_tile_ptr) at its cell (cell_ptrs), colours ($CAEE) and characters (monster_draw).

One of the four routines a blocked monster tries (turn_routines), each for one quarter of the facings: looks at the cells beside the monster's 2 x 2 block on the two sides that quarter faces (through turn_probe, or the wrapped cells at the map's right and bottom edges) and returns in $2A a bit for each blocked side; when neither side is blocked but the corner is, it gives one of the two, alternating each time (turn_alt_ul).
Which side turn_up_left gives when only the corner is blocked; flipped each time.
The same test for the next quarter of the facings, alternating through turn_alt_ur.
turn_up_right's alternating choice.
The same test for another quarter, alternating through turn_alt_dl.
turn_down_left's alternating choice.
The same test for the last quarter, alternating through turn_alt_dr.
turn_down_right's alternating choice.
Points $F7/$F8 at the character map cell of the position in $C357/$C358 and sets the carry when the position is inside the map's top-left $7B, where no wrapping is needed.
A zero byte after turn_probe.
The cell turn_probe looks at (X), one up and left of the monster.
Its Y.
The facing monster_aim and monster_turn settled on for this monster.
Clears the four character cells of the monster at cell_pos_x/cell_pos_y (cell_unplot), with the maze's wrap at the right and bottom edges.
Zeroes the four character map cells at ($F9).

A monster hits player X: on alternate attempts (bit 0 of its flags, toggled), the player loses health by the monster's level (monster_damage: 5, 8 or 10, in decimal), $C40C,x being raised when it runs out. Then the player may hit back (fight_back).
The health a monster's blow takes by its level, two bytes each (one per player): 5, 8, 10.
The health a ghost's touch takes by its level: 10, 20, 30.
Eleven bytes nothing in the traced code reads by name: 0 1 9 8 $0A 2 6 4 5 0 0 (the code at $C40E would use them).
Set when player one's health has run out; deaths takes it out of the game, and while it or dead_p2 is set the raster interrupt runs health_tick every frame.
Set when player two's health has run out.
27 bytes no traced code reaches: a routine that, after an attack, would set a bit for monster Y's facing in the table at $C40A.

A potion's blast on monster Y: the blast's player (blast_owner - 1) does its magic damage ($A00E,x) to the monster's strength; a monster with nothing left is removed and scores 10 (score_generator). Death (kind 5) always goes, scoring the next of death_scores for the player who used the potion.
Takes monster Y off the map (monster_unplot) and out of the table (the last monster into its slot, the count down); carry set.

After its move, a demon (kind 2) may fire (fireball_fire): once in four moves (a count in bits 6-7 of its flags), when the target player is straight in line with it on an axis or a diagonal. A lobber (kind 3) throws a rock at the same rate (rock_throw).
Work: the target's Y distance, compared with its X distance for a diagonal.
monster_shoot's lobber branch: the throw count in bits 6-7 of its flags, and rock_throw once in four moves.

After a monster's attack on player X, a player whose stick points at the monster (its facing, flipped when fleeing, through facing_stick) hits it: 25 points (fight_score) and the player's hand-to-hand damage ($ACCA,x) off its strength; with nothing left the monster dies (monster_kill). A ghost or Death cannot be fought. A blow that does not kill puts the idle timer back.
Adds 25 (decimal) to player X's score and raises panel_dirty.
For each facing, the stick bits that point that way, active low.
A ghost's touch on player X: the health its level takes (ghost_damage, in decimal), $C40C,x being raised when it runs out.
Blanks the screen: clears bit 4 of $D011 and of its copy $8252.
Shows the screen again: sets bit 4 of $D011 and $8252.
Selects the video chip's bank A (0-3) on CIA 2's port A ($DD00, bits 0-1 inverted, made outputs in $DD02).
Sets the screen's base in $D018's high nibble to A (in 1 KB steps within the bank).
Sets the character base in $D018 (bits 1-3) to A (in 2 KB steps).
Nine bytes no traced code reaches: sets bitmap mode (bit 5 of $D011).

Builds the level from the file at $0A00: the maze's look (maze_style), an empty tile grid (grid_clear), a wall along the top row (grid_top_wall) and, unless the maze wraps left and right, along the left column (grid_left_wall); then works through the wall commands ($0A03 bytes from $0A04): a pair of bytes starts a line at a tile with a kind (wall_start), and each byte after it draws a run of tiles in one of eight directions (wall_run); then the objects (objects_place). Each wall tile is joined to its neighbours as it goes in.
Clears the tile grid $0C00-$0FFF.
Fills the grid's top row with tile $0A, a straight wall.
Unless bit 7 of the header wraps the maze, puts a wall down the grid's left column: $0F at the top, $05 below.
Zero when the wall-command bytes at Y and Y + 1 have the same top three bits.

A two-byte wall command: the kind from the first byte's top three bits (wall_kind), the column from its low five bits, the row from the second's; points $8C/$8D at the tile and puts the first piece there (wall_plot).

A one-byte wall command: the top three bits are a direction (wall_steps), the low five one less than the run's length; each step puts a piece (wall_plot). A door or trap-wall line (kind $40 or $80) changes its kind by the direction (wall_kind_by_dir).
Puts a piece of the line's kind (wall_tiles: an exit $36, a door $11 or $12, a removable wall $90, a wall $10) at ($8C) and joins it to the wall on each side (wall_join, four times).
For side Y (the BIT instructions give the entries for 0, 4, 8 and 12: up, right, down, left): when the tile that way is a wall, each gets the other's join bit, so the brick pattern meets.
wall_join's entry for side 8 (down); the BIT instructions hide the other entries' loads.
wall_join's entry for side 4 (right).
wall_join's entry for side 0 (up), the start of the shared code.
Points $8E/$8F at the tile beside ($8C) in direction Y (wall_steps), wrapping at the grid's edges; carry clear when it is empty or a wall.

Unpacks the object section of the level file (after the wall commands, to the length in $0A00 with bit 7 of $0A02 as its ninth bit) into the tile grid from $0C00. A byte with bit 7 set skips (byte - $80 + 1) tiles. Any other byte is a tile, put once, or, when the next byte is below $13, that many + 2 times (place_tile). The monster count starts empty ($824E = $FF).
Counts one byte off the object section's length.

Puts the object tile (object_tile) at ($8C) and moves on: wall pieces are joined to their neighbours; an exit ($36) is counted (level_exits); a tile from $40 is a monster, added to the table (monster_from_level) and leaving the grid empty; $3F is the players' start (start_here).

Adds the monster tile at ($8C) to the monster table: its position from the tile address, its level from the tile's low two bits, its kind from bits 3-5 (Death, kind 5, always $C0), a random facing and random flags (CIA 1 timer A).
The players' start: notes the tile's grid address in $C0/$C1 and $C2/$C3, and its column and row in start_x and start_y.
For side Y (entries for 12, 8, 4, 0 by the BIT instructions): the wall beside loses its join bit for this side.
wall_unjoin_side's entry for side 8 (down).
wall_unjoin_side's entry for side 4 (right).
wall_unjoin_side's entry for side 0 (up), the start of the shared code.
The step in the 32 x 32 tile grid for each of the eight directions: -$20, -$1F, 1, $21, $20, $1F, -1, -$21.
wall_steps read from its second byte.
The join bit for each side, and the matching bit of the tile opposite: 4 1 8 2 1 4 2 8.
wall_join_bits read from its second byte: the opposite tile's bit.
The wall-command bytes still to read.
The exits in the level (counted as they are placed), and teleport_place's loop counter.
A tile column, for tile_at.
A tile row, for tile_at.
The kind of wall line being drawn (top three bits of its command).
$80 for a wall that a trap takes away, ORed into the pieces.
Bit 7 of the neighbouring tile.
Bit 7 of the tile beside, for wall_unjoin_side.
The tile each wall kind puts down: 0, an exit $36, a vertical door $11, 0, a horizontal door $12, 0, a removable wall $90, a wall $10.
The kind a door line takes by its direction: $40 $80 $40 $80.
How many more times place_tile puts the object.
The tile being placed.
The tile column of tile_at.
The tile row of tile_at.
Reads the tile at (tile_col, tile_row) of the grid into object_tile, without bit 7.

Points $F7/$F8 at the colour map and $F9/$FA at the character map for the tile at (tile_col, tile_row) (two cells per tile), and $FB/$FC, $FD/$FE at the tile's four characters ($F400 + tile x 4) and colours ($F600 + tile x 4).
Draws the monster's four characters at ($F9): straight (tile_plot) when its position is clear of the map's right and bottom edges, otherwise cell by cell through map_wrap_x.
Copies four characters from ($FB) into the 2 x 2 character map cells at ($F9).

Writes the monster's four colours from ($FD) into the colour map at ($F7): straight (colour_plot) unless its position is at the right edge, where the cells wrap. Both of its edge tests compare cell_pos_x; the bottom edge (cell_pos_y) is never tested.
Copies four colours from ($FD) into the 2 x 2 colour map cells at ($F7).

Colours the monster's four cells with one colour: from ($FD),3 cell by cell through map_wrap_x at the right edge, or ($FD),0 straight. Like monster_colour_wrapped, it tests cell_pos_x twice and never cell_pos_y.
Puts $5B in the monster's four character cells: an invisible sorcerer leaves its cells occupied (a character the maze font draws as floor) without drawing itself.
Draws the whole 32 x 32 tile grid into the character and colour maps, tile by tile (tile_at, tile_ptrs, tile_plot, colour_plot).
When bit 2 of the level header $0A01 is set, keeps one exit at random (a random number below the level's exit count, from the CIA 1 timers) and clears the others from the grid.
After levels 1 and 4 (level_number 2 or 5), turns the labelled exit tiles $37 and $38 into plain exits ($36); exit_targets then sends each to its level by its place.
Moves every Death (kind 5) to the front of the monster table, each with a drain count of 50 ($0700: 50 touches of 4, the 200 health the manual names).
Zero when monster Y is Death (kind bits $28).
Swaps monster Y with the next slot at the front of the table and gives it its drain count.
A JMP $CD77 no traced code reaches.
The sound effect on voice 1: $FF for none, otherwise the steps it has played.
The sound effect on voice 2.
The sound effect on voice 3.
The effect number on each voice.
Work: the step's first byte (the waveform choice in the low nibble, sustain/release in the high).
Work: the step's second byte (the pitch).
The voice sfx_start picked.
A zero byte before sfx_play.

Called from the raster interrupt every frame: for each voice with an effect, plays its next step (two bytes from the stream at $A6/$A7, $A8/$A9, $AA/$AB through sfx_note); a step whose first byte is 0 ends the effect, zeroing the voice's frequency. For voice 3 that zeroing goes to $D414/$D415 (its sustain/release and the filter's cutoff) instead of its frequency at $D40E/$D40F.
Stops every effect and sets the SID's 25 registers from sid_init.
43 bytes no traced code reaches: an older SID set-up (writing $D421-$D423 and $D418, gates off, pulse width $08).
The 25 values sfx_reset writes to $D400-$D418: pulse widths $08, volume $0F with the filter settings.

Starts sound effect A: while a tune plays it takes voice 1 (and stops the others' effects); otherwise a voice already playing the same effect, or a free one, or the one furthest through its effect. The effect's stream comes from the pointer table at $F000 (sfx_table, offsets from $F000).

Plays one step on the voice at offset Y: the pitch byte, inverted and shifted, into the frequency registers; the gate restarted with attack/decay 0 and a waveform chosen by the first byte's low nibble (noise $81 when it is set, pulse $41 when it is zero); sustain/release from its high nibble; pulse width $08.
23 bytes no traced code reaches: set or clear the border colour, and wait for the raster line to change.
Waits until every sound effect has ended and the tune player has stopped; then clears the music flag $8249.
Waits until no voice has an effect playing.
325 bytes no traced code reaches: a garbled older copy of the sound-effect code (with addresses in the $CDA5 range), then runs of noise and padding to $CFFC.
Set once the heroes' graphics have been copied (heroes_load_shapes); the start-up skips the file loading when it is set.
The heroes chosen on the selection screen, one byte per player (the selection program writes them here).

The music player's per-frame entry (file PLAYER-$E000): when music_on is set, runs one frame of the tune (music_frame) and copies the 25 shadow registers (sid_shadow) to the SID at $D400-$D418. level_intro calls it once a frame while the level jingle plays.
The music player's start entry: A/X give the tune's address (the level jingle is at $EA00), kept in $02/$03; goes to music_setup.

One frame of the tune: advances the tempo counter (music_tempo_frac + music_tempo, carrying into music_tempo_count), then for each of the three voices runs its commands, counts its note down and applies its effects (vibrato, slides, pulse sweep, arpeggio), keeping each voice's stream pointer in music_stream_lo/hi.
The low byte of the JSR at $E094, rewritten with the handler of the command being run (music_commands).
The high byte of that JSR's target.

Counts voice X's note down (music_note_count with music_note_long); near its end ($E640,x) it clears the gate bit in the shadow control register; when the note is over it resets the voice's effects and reads the next note: a byte of $80 or more is a pitch (plus the transposition $E5E6,x, turned into a frequency by music_freq, with the voice's other two arpeggio notes worked out the same way), 0 is a rest, and the byte after it is the length ($FF chains a tied note).

Starts a tune: clears the player's 126 bytes of state from $E585, sets the gate-off times to 2, each voice's note count and $E61D to 1, takes the three voices' stream addresses from the tune's header (offsets added to the tune's address), silences the shadow registers (music_silence) and turns music_on on.
